reviews.question: In a four-player standard game, how many Escape Pods are selected, how are they distributed and oriented, and which tokens start in the Intruder bag?

requested_parts.reason: Three randomly selected Pods.
Lowest in A, next B, third A.
All Locked side up.
Blank 1, Larvae 4, Creeper 1, Queen 1, Adults 7; arithmetic is supported.

reader_requested_parts: Number of Escape Pods selected in a four-player game.
How the selected Pods are distributed between Sections A and B.
The starting orientation of the Pods.
The exact tokens initially placed in the Intruder bag.
reviews.observed_answer: 1. Select 3 Escape Pod tokens for four players. 2. Put the lowest-numbered Pod in Section A, the next-numbered in Section B, then alternate A/B (so the third goes in A). 3. All Pods start Locked side up. 4. Put 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, and 3 Adults plus 1 additional Adult per player in the bag. At four players that is 7 Adults, 14 tokens total.
reviews.reader_evidence: 1–3. Setup states: “Take randomly chosen Escape Pod tokens: 2 pods for 1–2 players, 3 for 3–4 players, 4 for 5 players. Place the lowest-numbered pod in Section "A", the next (in numerical order) in Section "B", then alternate A/B. All pods start with their Locked side face up. Return the rest to the box.” 4. Setup states: “Put these Intruder tokens in the Intruder bag: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player. Place the remaining Intruder tokens and the Intruder Carcass tokens next to the board.” Inference: four players therefore means 3 + 4 = 7 Adult tokens and 1 + 4 + 1 + 1 + 7 = 14 tokens in total.
reviews.expected_answer: Three random pods; lowest numbered in A, next B, next A, all Locked. Bag: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 7 Adults.

No normal Actions; Interruption remains possible under its requirements.
Any number at the moment of passing.
No additional Fire wounds to this passed Character that turn.

reader_requested_parts: When the Character suffers Fire damage after taking one Action and passing.
Whether the Character may take normal Actions again this Player Phase.
Whether cards may be discarded on passing.
Whether later players' rounds cause additional Fire wounds to this passed Character.
reviews.observed_answer: 1. The Character takes 1 Light Wound at the end of their own passing round, after declaring Pass. 2. They cannot take further normal Actions for the rest of this Player Phase, though the general rule allows an Interruption card after passing subject to its requirements. 3. At the moment of passing, they may discard any number of cards from their hand. 4. Turn Structure says: “A Character who ends their round in a Room with a Fire marker suffers 1 Light Wound (every round; only after finishing their own round — passing players take it once at the end of their round and no more that turn).” The passing table says: “Fire in your Room | Take 1 Light Wound at the end of your own passing round. Later players' rounds do not give you further Fire wounds that turn.” FAQ says: “Fire applies at the end of your passing round, after you declare Pass.” 2. The passing table says: “Normal Actions | You cannot take further normal Actions; Interruption remains permitted as below.” It also says: “You may still play Interruption after passing, subject to its usual card requirements (FAQ Rules 21).” 3. The passing table says: “At the moment you pass, you may discard any number of cards from your hand.”
reviews.expected_answer: At end of own round take 1 Light Wound. Passing bars normal Actions this Player Phase, but official FAQ permits Interruption after passing. May discard any number of hand cards on passing. No further Fire wounds from later players rounds this turn.

reviews.question: Describe entering an empty unexplored Room: tile, Item Counter, Exploration effect, Noise roll and token destination. How do Silence, Danger and an already occupied destination alter the Noise roll?

requested_parts.reason: Flip tile and reveal Exploration token.
Rotate to token number, except Nest and Slime Room have no counter.
Resolve before ordinary movement Noise, including automatic Silence or Danger replacement.
Remove from game into box.
Roll for empty destination unless replaced by Silence or Danger.
No movement Noise roll if Character or Intruder is already present.

reader_requested_parts: What happens to an unexplored Room tile and its Item Counter on entry.
How its Exploration effect and token are resolved.
When and where the ordinary Movement Noise roll occurs, and how Silence/Danger affect it.
What happens to a Noise marker when its Corridor already has one.
How an already occupied destination affects the Movement Noise roll.
reviews.observed_answer: 1. On entering a face-down Room, flip the tile face up and reveal its Exploration token. The token's number sets the Item Counter for ordinary Rooms by rotating the tile until that number faces the board's Item Counter symbol; the Nest and Room Covered With Slime have no Item count. 2. Resolve the revealed effect, then remove the Exploration token from the game into the box. A Door effect places a Door token in the Corridor used to enter. 3. After exploration, make the ordinary Noise roll only if the destination has no Character or Intruder; the resulting number places a Noise marker in the corresponding connected Corridor (including a Technical Corridors Entrance if applicable). A Silence Exploration result replaces the Noise roll with no effect (unless the mover has Slime, when it resolves as Danger). A Danger result replaces the roll and moves all eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into the destination; if none are eligible, place Noise markers in each connected Corridor lacking one (including Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance). 4. If the numbered Corridor already has a Noise marker, resolve an Encounter instead of placing a second marker there. 5. If any Character or Intruder is already in the destination, do not roll Movement Noise.
reviews.reader_evidence: 1–2. Movement rules state: “After entering a Room: (1) if the Room tile was unexplored (face down), flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then return that token to the box; (2) apply the Movement Noise rule.” Exploration tokens state: “The token's front shows (1) a number = the amount of Items obtainable in that Room, and (2) a special effect symbol.” And: “the Nest and Room Covered With Slime get no Item count. For other Room tiles, rotate the tile until the Exploration token's number faces the Item Counter symbol printed on the board next to the slot.” Doors effect: “place a Door token in the Corridor by which you entered.” Token handling: “After resolving an Exploration token, remove it from the game into the box; it does not return to a supply or stay on the Room (each is resolved only once, on first entry).” 3. Movement rules state: “A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise again afterward. Otherwise, perform the ordinary Noise roll if the destination is empty (no Characters, no Intruders). If anyone — Character or Intruder — is already there, do NOT roll for Movement Noise.” Exploration effects state: “Silence — no Movement Noise roll. Nothing happens. If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve "Danger" instead.” “Danger — no Movement Noise roll. Move ALL eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into this Room (eligible means not in Combat with any Character). If there are none eligible, place a Noise marker in every Corridor connected to this Room that lacks one, counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance.” 4. Noise rules state: “A Corridor may never hold more than 1 Noise marker — if instructed to place a marker where one already is, resolve an Encounter instead.” 5. Noise rules state: “Remember: never roll for Noise when moving into a Room containing another Character or an Intruder.”
reviews.expected_answer: Reveal Room and Exploration token; set counter to token number except Nest/Slime Room; resolve effect and remove Exploration token from game. Roll Noise in empty Room unless Silence or Danger exploration cancels it. Occupied Room (Character or Intruder) gives no movement Noise roll.

reviews.question: You roll a number for a Corridor already holding Noise, with a Technical Corridors Entrance in your Room. Give the Encounter sequence, Noise removal, token destination and Surprise Attack comparison; do Contamination cards count?

All, including Technical Corridors with an Entrance.
Non-Blank kept aside; Blank uses its return procedure.
Hand count below token number causes attack against triggerer; evidence explicitly covers equal-or-more.

reader_requested_parts: What happens when a Noise roll calls for a Corridor that already has Noise.
Which connected Noise markers are removed and when.
How the Encounter draws and handles its token, including Blank versus non-Blank destinations.

reviews.observed_answer: 1. Since a Corridor cannot hold a second Noise marker, the attempted placement triggers an Encounter. 2. At the start of the Encounter, discard all Noise markers from Corridors connected to the Character's Room, including the Technical Corridors space because this Room has an Entrance. 3. Draw one Intruder token. If it is non-Blank, keep it aside outside the bag and place its matching miniature in the Room; it remains aside unless a rule returns it, such as that Intruder hiding in Technical Corridors. If it is Blank, instead place Noise in every Corridor connected to the Room, return the Blank to the bag, and end the Encounter without an Intruder appearing. 4. For a non-Blank token, compare its number with the number of cards in the triggering player's hand: fewer cards than that number causes a Surprise Attack. Action and Contamination cards both count, so the two Contamination cards in hand contribute to the comparison.
reviews.reader_evidence: 1. Noise rules state: “A Corridor may never hold more than 1 Noise marker — if instructed to place a marker where one already is, resolve an Encounter instead.” 2–3. Encounter rules state: “Discard ALL Noise markers from all Corridors connected to the Room (including Technical Corridors if there's an Entrance).” They continue: “Draw 1 Intruder token from the bag (symbol on one side, number on the other). Keep a non-Blank token aside outside the bag; it is not immediately returned. A Blank follows its separate return procedure below.” “Place the matching Intruder miniature in the Room.” “Blank token in an Encounter: place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to that Room. If the Blank was the LAST token in the bag: add 1 Adult token to the bag (if any are available; otherwise nothing). Return the Blank token to the bag. The Encounter ends (no miniature appears).” Technical Corridors rules state: “If an Intruder moves to a Technical Corridors Entrance, it disappears into the ducts: discard all its Injury markers, return its token to the Intruder bag, and remove its miniature from the board.” 4. Encounter rules state: “Compare the token's number to the number of cards in the triggering player's hand (Action AND Contamination cards both count). Fewer cards than the number → Surprise Attack (an Intruder Attack against that Character). Equal or more → nothing happens.” The Quick Reference likewise says the drawn non-Blank token is kept aside “until a rule returns it, such as an Intruder hiding in Technical Corridors.”
reviews.expected_answer: Resolve Encounter: remove all connected Noise including Technical Corridors; draw bag token; place matching Intruder; compare token number to all cards in triggering hand including Contamination. Fewer cards causes Surprise Attack against triggerer, equal or more does not. Set token aside.

The reference to two Contamination cards is an unsupported incidental scenario assumption, not a material change to the correctly stated hand-count rule; it is flagged separately.
